---
title: "Getting Started"
---

## Installation

Clone the repository and install dependencies:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/JDeleon2342/nba_api-project.git
cd nba_api-project
uv sync
```

## Using the API

Our project provides a Python API to access and analyze NBA shot data.

### Load Shot Data

```python
from src.data_collection import load_shot_data, load_team_metrics
shots   = load_shot_data()
metrics = load_team_metrics()
```

### Load Team Metrics

```python
from src.data_collection import load_dataset

metrics = load_dataset("data/team_metrics_clean.csv")
print(metrics.head())
```

## Running the Analysis

Execute analysis functions from the `src.analysis` module:

```python
from src.analysis import three_point_rate_by_season, rank_teams_by_three_point_adoption
from src.data_collection import load_dataset

shots = load_dataset("data/shot_data_clean.csv")

# League-wide three-point trend
trend = three_point_rate_by_season(shots)
print(trend)

# Teams ranked by adoption
rankings = rank_teams_by_three_point_adoption(shots)
print(rankings.head(10))
```

## Viewing Visualizations

Use the Streamlit app to interactively explore the data. This is hosted on the link in the Home page but can also be run with this command:

```bash
uv run streamlit run app.py
```

Then open your browser to `http://localhost:8501`.


## Complete Example — End to End Walkthrough

Here is a full example that loads the data, runs analysis, and produces a visualization:

```python
from src.data_collection import load_shot_data, load_team_metrics
from src.analysis import (
    three_point_rate_by_season,
    biggest_zone_shifts,
    rank_teams_by_three_point_adoption,
    correlate_three_pt_rate_with_wins
)
from src.visualization import (
    plot_three_point_trend,
    plot_zone_shift_bar,
    plot_top_three_point_adopters
)
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Step 1 — Load data
shots   = load_shot_data()
metrics = load_team_metrics()

# Step 2 — League wide three point trend
trend = three_point_rate_by_season(shots)
print(trend)

# Step 3 — Which zones changed most
shifts = biggest_zone_shifts(shots)
print(shifts)

# Step 4 — Which teams adopted three point shooting most
rankings = rank_teams_by_three_point_adoption(shots)
print(rankings.head(10))

# Step 5 — Does three point rate correlate with winning
corr_df = correlate_three_pt_rate_with_wins(shots, metrics)

# Step 6 — Visualize
fig = plot_three_point_trend(shots)
plt.show()

fig = plot_zone_shift_bar(shots)
plt.show()

fig = plot_top_three_point_adopters(shots, top_n=10)
plt.show()
```

### Expected Output

Running `three_point_rate_by_season(shots)` produces a DataFrame like:

| season | total_attempts | three_pt_attempts | three_pt_rate |
|--------|---------------|-------------------|---------------|
| 2013-14 | 198432 | 40123 | 20.2% |
| 2016-17 | 205341 | 52847 | 25.7% |
| 2019-20 | 187234 | 63421 | 33.9% |
| 2023-24 | 210543 | 82341 | 39.1% |

Running `rank_teams_by_three_point_adoption(shots)` produces:

| team | rate_first | rate_last | change |
|------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| Houston Rockets | 28.4% | 49.2% | +20.8% |
| Milwaukee Bucks | 22.1% | 42.3% | +20.2% |
| Golden State Warriors | 29.3% | 47.1% | +17.8% |
